cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Really Happened?
cards.instruction: Find the truth by comparing details, repeating questions, and testing which parts of the story remain consistent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For this missing-parcel form: was it a bag or a box? You've said both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A bag, I think. I carried it by the handles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Describe the handles. Were they attached to fabric or cardboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Cardboard. It had a rigid lid, too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why 'bag'? Tell me again what you carried. Was the box inside something?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're claiming for your lost bag. At four, were you on the bus or buying coffee? You've told me both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coffee. Can we finish the form?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the bag beside you when you paid?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. The driver waited while I ran in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So both fit. Tell me the boarding bit again: did the bag come back out with you?

cards.title: Back My Version
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to remember, repeat, and defend one shared version of events when questions begin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The allotment committee's asking about the greenhouse. We arrived after the glass broke, remember? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saw your wheelbarrow hit it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. We came inside afterwards. Can we both tell them we were clearing up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll say that. I won't lie about the wheelbarrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then start with clearing up. If they ask about the barrow, we moved it away afterwards. Let's both use that order.

cards.title: Test the Story First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to repeat the explanation, ask the dangerous question, or test the risky step before you commit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Try this banking-delay explanation for the missing raffle money on the chair before I sign it. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not defending your accounts again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Just test the explanation. If she accepts it, I'll sign and handle every question.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll recognise your handwriting before I speak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the paper. Ask whether a banking delay sounds plausible. If she asks whose money, come back before answering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try this banking-delay explanation for the missing raffle money on the chair before I sign it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not defending your accounts again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just test the explanation. If she accepts it, I'll sign and handle every question.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll recognise your handwriting before I speak.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the paper. Ask whether a banking delay sounds plausible. If she asks whose money, come back before answering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask Dad why our holiday account's empty. I'll wait by the kitchen door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come with me. You booked the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask whether he's angry about the price first. If he isn't, I'll come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm calling you in if he wants the flight receipt.

beats.text: Ask whether he wants the total or the breakdown before you call me. The seat upgrades need a longer explanation.

beats.text: Beside found, not beside attended.

beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Mum's asking who broke her vase. Will you tell her, or keep your promise to your little brother? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's blaming the cleaner. I can't let that happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Clear the cleaner. Do you have to name me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are you answering her, or keeping the promise I trusted you with?

beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum's asking who broke her vase. Will you tell her, or keep your promise to your little brother?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's blaming the cleaner. I can't let that happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Clear the cleaner. Do you have to name me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are you answering her, or keeping the promise I trusted you with?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The client asked who wrote our pitch. Will you tell her I copied it, or protect our partnership?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can withdraw it together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll withdraw it. Will you keep my name out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked whether you copied it. Withdrawing doesn't answer her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then before you say yes, decide whether we're still partners when she puts down the phone.
